outputs.L1: An object of the present invention is to provide an organic thin-film transistor capable of achieving high mobility, as well as a method for manufacturing the organic thin-film transistor. This object is achieved by providing a base material, a gate electrode, a gate insulating layer, an organic semiconductor layer, a source electrode, and a drain electrode. Charge injection layers are further provided between the source electrode and a layer located on the base-material side of the source electrode, and between the drain electrode and a layer located on the base-material side of the drain electrode. On the side of the source electrode facing the drain electrode and the side of the drain electrode facing the source electrode, the thickness of each charge injection layer decreases in a direction opposite to the direction in which the source and drain electrodes face each other. The source and drain electrodes are formed by scanning a metal layer with a laser, and a solution that forms the charge injection layers is added dropwise to the laser-scanned portion.
outputs.L2: The aim is to produce a high-mobility organic thin-film transistor and to provide a process for manufacturing it. This is accomplished by forming a device that includes a substrate, gate electrode, gate-insulating layer, organic semiconductor layer, source electrode, and drain electrode. Charge-injection layers are positioned between each of the source and drain electrodes and the respective underlying layer on the substrate side. At the mutually facing sides of the source and drain electrodes, the thickness of each charge-injection layer gradually diminishes in the direction away from the other electrode. The source and drain electrodes are created by laser-scanning a metal layer, after which a solution capable of forming the charge-injection layers is deposited dropwise onto the laser-treated region.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to an organic thin-film transistor configured to provide high charge-carrier mobility. The transistor includes a base material on which a gate electrode, a gate-insulating layer, an organic semiconductor layer, a source electrode, and a drain electrode are arranged.

Charge-injection layers are disposed beneath both the source electrode and the drain electrode to facilitate the injection of charge carriers into the organic semiconductor layer. Each charge-injection layer has a tapered thickness profile, such that its thickness decreases with increasing distance from the mutually facing sides of the source and drain electrodes. This configuration promotes efficient charge injection in the region between the electrodes and contributes to improved transistor performance.

The source and drain electrodes are formed by first providing a metal layer and selectively scanning the metal layer with a laser. A solution containing material for forming the charge-injection layers is then deposited dropwise onto the laser-scanned portions. The deposited solution forms the tapered charge-injection layers beneath the respective source and drain electrodes, thereby producing an organic thin-film transistor capable of achieving high charge-carrier mobility.
outputs.L4:
An organic thin-film transistor and a method for manufacturing the same are provided to improve charge injection and achieve high carrier mobility. The transistor includes a substrate, source and drain electrodes spaced apart from one another to define a channel region, an organic semiconductor layer, and charge-injection layers disposed between the source and drain electrodes and the underlying functional layer or layers. Each charge-injection layer has a tapered profile, with its thickness gradually decreasing toward the gap between the source and drain electrodes.

In the manufacturing method, a metal electrode layer is formed on the substrate and selectively scanned with a laser to define or modify regions corresponding to the source and drain electrodes. A solution containing a charge-injection material is then deposited on the laser-scanned regions. Differences in surface properties created by the laser treatment control the spreading, wetting, or accumulation of the solution, thereby forming charge-injection layers having the desired tapered shape.

The gradual reduction in thickness toward the electrode gap provides a smoother transition from the metal electrodes to the transistor channel. This structure reduces the interfacial barrier and contact resistance that can otherwise hinder the injection of charge carriers from the source electrode into the organic semiconductor layer. It also avoids an abrupt step at the electrode edge, which may cause discontinuities or defects in subsequently formed layers.

As a result, charge carriers can be injected more efficiently into the channel and transported between the source and drain electrodes. The improved electrode-channel interface enables the organic thin-film transistor to exhibit increased field-effect mobility, more stable electrical characteristics, and potentially lower operating voltage. The process is also compatible with solution-based deposition and localized laser patterning, making it suitable for the fabrication of flexible, lightweight, or large-area organic electronic devices.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Although it is short and easy to overlook, it plays an important role in communication. As the definite article, “the” points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can mean any book, while “the book” refers to a particular one.

The word also helps create shared understanding. When someone says, “Close the door,” both speaker and listener usually know which door is meant. In this way, “the” makes language clearer and more precise.

Small words often carry great importance, and “the” is a perfect example. It may contain only three letters, but without it, English would sound very different.

counterfactuals.output:
**Rewritten key claim:**

An organic semiconductor device comprising source and drain electrodes formed by laser processing, a charge-injection layer disposed in electrical contact with at least one of the electrodes, and an organic semiconductor layer arranged to conduct charge between the source and drain electrodes, wherein the charge-injection layer facilitates charge transfer from the laser-formed electrode into the organic semiconductor layer.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a single-paragraph technical description of an organic thin-film transistor structure designed to achieve high charge-carrier mobility, including its fabrication method.
counterfactuals.output: A high-mobility organic thin-film transistor can employ a bottom-gate, top-contact architecture consisting of a heavily doped silicon gate, a thermally grown SiO₂ dielectric modified with an alkylsilane self-assembled monolayer to reduce interfacial trap density, and a highly ordered organic semiconductor layer such as C8-BTBT or DNTT, followed by low-resistance gold source and drain electrodes. Fabrication begins with solvent cleaning and oxygen-plasma treatment of the Si/SiO₂ substrate, after which the dielectric is functionalized using vapor- or solution-phase silanization; the semiconductor is then deposited by slow thermal evaporation, solution shearing, or zone casting under controlled temperature and atmosphere to produce large, preferentially aligned crystalline domains along the source–drain direction. Gold contacts are patterned through a shadow mask or by lift-off, optionally using a contact-modifying interlayer to reduce the injection barrier, and the device is annealed in an inert atmosphere and encapsulated to suppress oxygen and moisture degradation. The combination of a smooth, low-trap dielectric interface, aligned molecular packing, minimal grain-boundary density, short channel geometry, and optimized electrode energetics enables efficient charge injection and high field-effect mobility.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain how tapered charge injection layers are arranged between the electrodes and underlying layers in this organic transistor, and mention the laser scanning and dropwise solution deposition steps.
counterfactuals.output:
Tapered charge-injection layers are interposed at the source and drain contacts, between each electrode and the underlying organic semiconductor stack. They are thicker beneath the electrode/contact region and gradually thin toward the channel, providing a smooth transition that lowers the carrier-injection barrier without significantly obstructing channel transport.

In fabrication, a laser is scanned over the intended contact regions to locally form or modify the tapered injection layers. The organic semiconductor or other solution-processable layer is then deposited dropwise onto the prepared structure and allowed to spread or dry, completing the transistor stack.
